assertions.name: abelian_rs_torsion_is_covolume_not_count
assertions.source: Vol(J)=√det G varies with lattice shape while b₁=d fixed => RS torsion is a covolume (1/Area category, data-excluded), not the bare count b₁; abelian RT route does not give 1/(π b₁)

description: Front-3 continuation of #3842 (which pruned the flat-torus determinant route and named the RT μ-prescription as the wall). Decisive bounded step on the ABELIAN side: does the U(1)-photon RT / Ray–Singer torsion normalization on the Jacobian J(M)=H¹/H¹(ℤ) carry a bare COUNT b₁ or a COVOLUME D? Structural fact: the abelian RS torsion of the trivial U(1) connection is the covolume Vol(J)=√det G (period/intersection Gram) — a b₁-dim VOLUME, shape-dependent, NOT the integer b₁. Demonstrated across 4 lattices: the covolume varies continuously (0.9..6.5-scale) while b₁=d is a fixed integer ⇒ RS torsion is a covolume, in the 1/Area category (data-EXCLUDED at −1419 ppb). So the abelian RT route does NOT give 1/(π b₁) either. The only count-b₁ object stays ζ_{Δ₁}(0)=−b₁ (area-free, #3834), and neither the flat-torus det (μ^{−b₁}) nor the RS torsion (covolume) turns it into the reciprocal 1/b₁. CONSEQUENCE: 1/(π b₁) is not an abelian-normalization object; the reciprocal-count 1/b₁ requires the b₁-democratic per-mode weight — the nonabelian RT S-matrix route (Front 2 / W_λ) or an independent prescription. Scope-(a) route-narrowing; no α_k wired; no fit; does NOT manufacture 1/(π b₁); 1/(8π) stays a phase-4 id.
